reconcile.note: Clarke reconciles the differing drink accounts by positing two or three separate cups offered before and during the crucifixion, so each evangelist describes a different moment.

discrepancy.note: Strauss shows all four gospels report a drink offered, but only Matthew and Mark disagree on its very composition before any timing question arises.

quotes.text: The presentation to Jesus of a drink mingled with vinegar is mentioned by all four, and even the two who have the vinegar mingled with gall, or the myrrhed wine, as the first drink offered to Jesus, mention afterwards the offering of simple vinegar.
quotes.attr: David Friedrich Strauss (d. 1874), The Life of Jesus Critically Examined (1846), on Matthew 27:34 and Mark 15:23.

sides.snippet: They gave him sour wine to drink mixed with gall. When he had tasted it, he would not drink.
sides.verseText: They gave him sour wine to drink mixed with gall. When he had tasted it, he would not drink.

sides.snippet: They offered him wine mixed with myrrh to drink, but he didn't take it.
